clauses.reason: Paragraph 1, with the authority recital, creates the President's Commission on Migratory Labor of a Chairman and four members designated by the President. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 2 authorizes and directs the Commission to inquire into five listed subjects, (a) to (e), on migratory workers. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 3 requires a written report to the President “not later than December 15,1950” (the held text has no space after the comma), with recommendations. Executive Order 10192 amended the date to March 1, 1951. The report date is a deadline and not an end; the clause continues until the Commission ceases to exist. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 4 authorizes public hearings and the hearing of witnesses. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 5 directs the Commission to consult the Department of State on matters involving international arrangements and policies. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 6 authorizes and directs executive departments and agencies to cooperate with the Commission and furnish information and assistance. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

The first piece of paragraph 7 provides that during the fiscal year 1950 the compensation of the members, including traveling expenses and per-diem allowances, and the Commission's expenditures are to be paid as the following page states. The page break splits the sentence. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

The second piece of paragraph 7 completes the funding sentence: the expenditures are paid from an allotment by the President from the Emergency Fund for the President appropriation of 1950, and the fiscal year 1951 compensation and expenditures are paid similarly from the corresponding 1951 appropriation, without regard to listed sections of the Revised Statutes. The paragraph funds the Commission and has no operation once the Commission has ceased to exist. It continues until the Commission ceases to exist; Executive Order 10236 provides that the Commission ceases to exist “at the end of May 31,1951”, so the clause ends on May 31, 1951.

Paragraph 8 originally read “Thirty days after rendition of its report to the President, the Commission shall cease to exist unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order.” Executive Order 10192 changed “Thirty days” to “Sixty days”. Executive Order 10236 then replaced the paragraph with “The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951.” Before and after: a report-relative cessation clause became a fixed-date cessation clause; the substance of the cessation clause changed and the clause was restated under the owner ruling on restatements. The clause is the cessation provision itself and ends on the day it fixes, May 31, 1951.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10129 (15 FR 3499 (Federal Register of June 6, 1950)) was signed June 3, 1950. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date; the text breaks across a page after paragraph 7 and resumes on a later page of the same issue, so paragraph 7 appears in two pieces. It creates the President's Commission on Migratory Labor (paragraph 1), directs it to inquire into five subjects (paragraph 2), requires a written report by December 15, 1950 (paragraph 3), authorizes hearings (paragraph 4), directs consultation with the Department of State (paragraph 5), directs agency cooperation (paragraph 6), provides funding for the fiscal years 1950 and 1951 from the Emergency Fund for the President (paragraph 7) and provides in paragraph 8 that the Commission ceases to exist thirty days after its report unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated on May 31, 1951, the day the Commission ceased to exist. Executive Order 10192 (15 FR 9029 (Federal Register of December 19, 1950)), signed December 15, 1950, amended paragraph 3 (the report date becomes March 1, 1951) and paragraph 8 (“Thirty days” becomes “Sixty days”). Executive Order 10236 (16 FR 3607 (Federal Register of April 27, 1951)), signed April 26, 1951, amended paragraph 8 as amended to read “The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951.”, which fixes the end. The report date of paragraph 3 and the report-relative cessation of paragraph 8 are not ends: the held corpus does not give the date the report was rendered, and Executive Order 10236 replaced the report-relative rule with a fixed date while the Commission still existed. Executive Order 10193's Federal Register page contains the text of Executive Order 10192 and cites Executive Order 10129 only for that reason; it is not a separate amendment. The held-text search for citations of the order found only Executive Orders 10192, 10236 and their page copies. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists two hits (the 10192 and 10236 amendments); the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit.
